home_story_1: Two months ago I read the blog post “{post}” by Stepan Parunashvili about turning an iPhone into a dumbphone with Apple Configurator. I tried it. The setup was fine; the effort is a part of why it holds. But that setup had some serious problems.
home_story_2: The App Store was off, so nothing updated. I couldn't log in to my bank app. The web was an allow list, so I could not even scan a QR menu at a restaurant. The configuration part is done via Apple Configurator manually by clicking buttons. I realized using Apple Configurator isn't even necessary. So I built a guide that keeps the App Store on, blocks the apps even if they're installed, blocks their URLs, and leaves the rest of the phone alone.
home_story_3: I met a lot of people lately. Per my observations, most of people's problems come down to not being able to do hard things. When I check their screen time I mostly saw 6 hours and more.
home_story_4: People do anything to escape the hard work. And having an infinite amusement machine on their fingertips makes this a thousand times easier.
home_story_5: I think I finally fixed this for myself and I wanted to turn my expertise into a non-profit social awareness project.
home_story_6: That is the whole reason this site exists. If more people try blocking these distracting apps, we could learn more, experiment more and share more.
home_story_7: I used the time I got from Instagram reels to build this website as the ultimate example.
home_story_8: We should get better at protecting ourselves and our next generations from a system built to farm attention.
home_story_9: It is not only the hours. It is what the hours do. You stop doing hard things. You stop getting better at anything. The muscle goes soft and you become a cog. I wanted a way out that does not depend on willpower, because mine runs out by afternoon like everyone else's.
home_story_10: Most people will close this tab. That is fine. This is for the ones who will be glad they found it, the way I was glad I found that blog post.
home_how_app_body: Plug the iPhone in with a cable. The app backs it up, flips one flag inside the backup and restores it. The phone comes back supervised with everything still on it, and the feed apps and their sites blocked by a profile that cannot be removed. It takes about 45 minutes, erases nothing, costs nothing, and needs an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or newer.
home_how_undo: Unsupervise the same way, from the same app.
home_faq_supervision_desc: A device mode Apple built for schools and companies. A supervised iPhone accepts settings a normal one refuses: hiding apps, and a profile that cannot be removed. Everything else about the phone stays the same.
home_faq_see_term: Can the supervisor see my phone?
home_faq_see_desc: No. Supervision is a flag, not a connection. Remote control needs an MDM server, and you enrol in none. The app runs on your own Mac and sends nothing. The profile is a fixed file: once installed, nobody can change it or read anything back.
home_faq_erase_term: Do I have to erase my iPhone?
home_faq_erase_desc: No. Apple's way erases. The app supervises from a local backup: it backs the phone up to your Mac, patches one flag, restores it. Photos, messages and logins stay.
home_faq_data_desc: No. The app patches a backup and restores it to the same phone. Apps re-download; an encrypted backup carries your saved passwords, Health data and keychain, so fewer of them ask you to log in again. Keep a local backup on your Mac anyway. It is faster than iCloud and you can restore it in one click.
home_faq_undo_desc: Yes. The same app takes supervision back off: plug the phone in and it backs up, flips the flag the other way and restores. Erasing the phone also removes supervision; restore from iCloud or your local backup after.
home_faq_change_term: Can I change the profile later?
home_faq_change_desc: You can always add restrictions by installing another profile. You cannot loosen or remove one without erasing the phone. Start with the recommended list; add later if needed. Each install is a new profile; installing another one adds to what is already blocked. Want to try first? Turn on trial mode in the app and the profile stays removable.
home_faq_updates_term: Will my banking apps keep updating?
home_faq_updates_desc: Yes. The App Store stays on. Only the apps you list disappear.
home_faq_keep_term: What about WhatsApp, Maps, my bank?
home_faq_keep_desc: Untouched. You choose the list. We only suggest the feeds.
home_faq_apple_desc: It uses Apple's own configuration profiles and backup format. The no-wipe supervision trick is not documented by Apple; it works on iOS 26.6.1 today.
home_faq_mac_desc: You need a Mac once, for about an hour: Apple Silicon, macOS 14 or newer. Borrow one. The phone needs no Mac afterwards.
home_faq_android_desc: Not yet. Android has no settings file like this; blocking that holds needs a small device-owner app, which is a different build. We plan to add it. Until then this site is iPhone only, and Digital Wellbeing limits still rely on your willpower.
home_faq_windows_term: Does it work from a Windows PC?
home_faq_windows_desc: Not yet. The app runs on a Mac today. Windows makes the same backup through iTunes, so support is planned. Until then, borrow a Mac once; the phone needs no computer afterwards.
home_faq_who_desc: Mert Duzgun, a developer in Antalya. This is not a business. The code is public, the profile is signed with my Apple developer certificate, and nothing you do here is tracked.

guides_lead: How to take your attention back, written out: the browser half of it, site by site, for people who want to understand it first.
guides_description: A guide to taking your attention back on the computer: use social media with the feeds cut out of X, YouTube, Instagram and TikTok.
guides_ext_title: Use social media from your computer, not your phone
guides_ext_summary: The browser half of the same idea: the feeds come out of X, YouTube, Instagram and TikTok, and the accounts stay where you can work.
ext_privacy_lead: The attention awareness extension hides feeds with CSS. It collects nothing.
ext_privacy_stores_body: Your switches (on or off per site) and the custom CSS rules you write, in the browser's extension storage.
ext_privacy_stores_sync: If you are signed into your browser, the browser may sync that storage across your devices. Nothing else.
ext_privacy_sends_body: Nothing. No analytics, no crash reports, no remote code, no network requests of its own.
ext_privacy_sees_body: The pages on x.com, youtube.com, instagram.com and tiktok.com, only to inject CSS.
ext_privacy_sees_custom: If you add a custom rule for another site, the browser asks you once for access to that site. The extension then injects your CSS there and nothing more.
ext_privacy_source_body: The code is public at {repo}, and the rules are plain CSS files you can read.
guide_ext_head_title: Use social media from your computer, not your phone
guide_ext_title: Use social media from your computer, not your phone
guide_ext_description: The phone is a slot machine in your pocket. A computer is a desk you get up from. The attention awareness extension cuts the feeds out of X, YouTube, Instagram and TikTok so the browser stays a tool.
guide_ext_intro: The profile takes the apps off the iPhone. This is the other half: a browser extension that removes the feeds from the four sites that carry them, and leaves the rest of each site alone.
guide_ext_why_1: The phone is a slot machine in my pocket. It is always there, the feed is vertical, and one thumb runs it, so a minute of waiting turns into forty with no decision anywhere in the middle.
guide_ext_why_2: A computer is a desk. I sit down at it, I do the thing I came for, and then I get up and leave. Same accounts, same people, same posts, but the room has a door.
guide_ext_why_3: Once the apps are blocked on the iPhone, the computer is where I still post, message, search and watch the channels I chose. The extension cuts the feeds out of the four sites so the computer stays a tool rather than the phone with a bigger screen. Those are the same hours a day {bill} bills you for over the next twenty years.
guide_ext_why_bill_link: the bill on the home page
guide_ext_install_title: Add it from the Chrome Web Store
guide_ext_install_body: One click: {store}. The aa mark lands in the toolbar; pin it and the switches are one click away.
guide_ext_install_store_link: add attention awareness to your browser
guide_ext_install_browsers: It works in Chrome, Brave, Edge and any other Chromium browser.
guide_ext_install_privacy: It collects nothing: no account, no analytics, no server, and nothing leaves the machine. What it stores and what it can see is written out on the {privacy}.
guide_ext_sites_body: Site by site, taken from the rule files, which are plain CSS with a header that says what each one hides and what it leaves alone.
guide_ext_x_gone_1: The For you tab on the home timeline
guide_ext_x_gone_3: The today's news box in the sidebar
guide_ext_x_stays_3: Search, and the Explore tab it lives behind
guide_ext_yt_gone_1: Every Shorts surface: the shelves on home, subscriptions, search and watch
guide_ext_yt_gone_2: The Shorts entry in both sidebars, and the Shorts tab on a channel
guide_ext_yt_gone_3: The /shorts/ player itself, which gets a short note in its place
guide_ext_ig_gone_1: Reels, and the Reels entry in the nav
guide_ext_ig_gone_2: The Explore grid and its tabs
guide_ext_ig_gone_3: The suggested for you blocks, in the sidebar and in the feed
guide_ext_ig_gone_4: The For you tab on the home feed
guide_ext_tt_gone_1: All of it. TikTok is a feed with a site drawn around it, so the page goes and a short note takes its place
guide_ext_switches_site: One switch per site in the popup. Off means the stylesheet is gone from that site, not that something is hiding behind a setting.
guide_ext_switches_master: One master switch over the four turns all of them off at once.
guide_ext_switches_custom: Custom CSS, on the options page, is the Stylus-shaped part: a domain, a block of CSS, applied on top of the built-in rules. Hide whatever bothers you on any other site.
guide_ext_switches_domain: A domain covers its subdomains, so reddit.com covers old.reddit.com.
guide_ext_switches_permission: A site outside the four asks the browser for access to that one site as you add the rule, once, and for nothing else.
guide_ext_switches_example_body: Say a news site keeps a trending sidebar next to the article. Open the browser's inspector, read the class off the element, and give the options page those two things.
